This example runs the real assistant: a workspace with one Familiar, its memory and tools, and a DM to talk to it in. The model is scripted and the storage lives in memory, so you need no credentials or network.

```sh
npm install @familiar-ai/core @familiar-ai/client
```

Familiar needs Node 24.19 or newer. Save this as `first-familiar.ts` and run it with `node first-familiar.ts`:

<Code code={firstFamiliar} lang="ts" title="first-familiar.ts" />

It prints the DM:

```text
Sam: Hello
Familiar: Hello, Sam.
```

## What each part does

- **`fauxProvider`** is a scripted model: each `setResponses` entry answers one request. Use it in tests. For a demo that answers every request, use `scriptedModels` from `@familiar-ai/core/models/scripted`.
- **`MemoryStorage`** keeps everything in memory until the process exits.
- **`openWorkspace`** opens the workspace, resumes unfinished work and starts background work such as schedules and memory filing.
- **`familiars.create`** makes a Familiar. A lasting host does this once, on the first open.
- **`rooms.dm`** gets or creates the DM between a Familiar and a person, by your ID for them.
- **`post`** records a message and starts the Familiar's turn. Reuse the `requestId` if you retry the same message, so it's posted once.
- **`watch`** returns the room's log, then each commit, so you see the reply arrive.
- **`ConversationTranscript`** assembles the log, and **`toRoomTranscript`**, from the client package, turns it into chat items. It's pure, so it works on the server too.
- **`dismiss`** closes the workspace. Always call it, so timers and connections stop.

## Make it last

Two things change for a real assistant:

1. **Persistent storage.** On Node, use `openNodeSqliteStorage` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node`. Install the exact Pi Durable version that core depends on, because Pi's storage format and types change between releases. On Workers, use [@familiar-ai/cloudflare](/familiar/build/cloudflare/).
2. **A real model.** Register a provider and give it credentials. That's the next page, [Models and sign-in](/familiar/build/models-and-sign-in/).
